title: A boon beyond the three: the fire named for Naciketas
theme: Pleased, Death gives an extra boon: the fire will bear Naciketas’s name, and he is given a many-formed chain.

words.gram: pres. middle participle m. nom. sg.

words.context: Śaṅkara: «महात्मा अक्षुद्रबुद्धिः» — of no petty mind
Śaṅkara: «वरं तव चतुर्थम् इह प्रीतिनिमित्तम् अद्य इदानीं ददामि भूयः पुनः प्रयच्छामि» — a fourth boon
Śaṅkara: «सृङ्कां शब्दवतीं रत्नमयीं मालाम्» — a jewelled, tinkling chain

sandhi.type: m before a vowel; t before p
sandhi.rule: Final m stays before a vowel; final t before p stays.
aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes o: P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) with P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः).

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: ā + a → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः); m stays before a vowel.

samasa.meaning: one whose self is great, magnanimous

morphology.note: Present participle of the passive stem of prī ‘be pleased’ (prīyate): ‘being pleased’.
Present of dā. Madhva’s text and Raṅgarāmānuja read ददानि (imperative-subjunctive 1 sg., ‘let me give’).
A rare word. Śaṅkara gives two senses: a jewelled chain, and, alternatively, a good path, the way of action: «यद्वा, सृङ्काम् अकुत्सितां गतिं कर्ममयीं गृहाण».

translation.literal: ‘The great-souled one, being pleased, said to him: “Here, now, I give you a boon again: this fire will be [known] by your name indeed. And take this chain of many forms.”’
translation.readable: ‘Delighted, the great-hearted Death said to him: “I give you one more gift here and now. This fire will be called by your name. And take this chain of many colours.”’

syntax: A narrative frame (tam abravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā) and Death’s speech: the extra boon (varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ) and its content in two parts, the naming of the fire and the gift of the chain, with the imperative gṛhāṇa.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: a tinkling jewelled chain, or alternatively the good way of action: «यद्वा, सृङ्काम् अकुत्सितां गतिं कर्ममयीं गृहाण». Raṅgarāmānuja: a tinkling string of jewels, «शब्दवती रत्नमालां स्वीकुरु». Madhva: golden, «अनेकरूपां सुवर्णमयीम्» (see the commentary).
Madhva’s text and Raṅgarāmānuja’s read dadāni, ‘let me give’; the base and the other witnesses dadāmi, ‘I give’ (corrections.json).

metre.name: triṣṭubh
metre.note: Counted as written, 22 and 23 syllables: the second line (tavaiva nāmnā bhavitāyam agniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemām anekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa) has one syllable more than the norm.

beginner: Death is so pleased with his student that he adds a gift that was not asked for. From now on, he says, this fire ritual will be known by your name — the Nāciketa fire. And he gives the boy a chain or necklace of many forms. The gift of a name means that whenever people perform the ritual they will remember the boy who learned it from Death. The chain is a prize, the kind a teacher gives a brilliant pupil. Some commentators also read it as a sign of the many paths of action now open to him.
analogy: Like a professor who names a theorem after the student who first understood it, and hands over a medal as well.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Two things: the fire will be called by Naciketas’s name, and he is given a many-formed chain.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: Death, seeing the pupil’s fitness, gives a fourth boon out of pleasure: «शिष्यस्य योग्यतां पश्यन्प्रीयमाणः प्रीतिमनुभवन्» … «वरं तव चतुर्थम्». Raṅgarāmānuja agrees: «पुनः चतुर्थं वरं ददानि».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: His comment on 1.1.12–18 is one passage, filed at 1.1.18. He glosses ‘of many forms’ as golden, «अनेकरूपां सुवर्णमयीम्», and cites a verse he attributes to the Pādma: Yama, pleased by the repetition, gave the fire its name and a golden neck-chain: «यमोऽनुवादसन्तुष्टो वह्नेस्तन्नामतामपि । शृङ्कां स्वर्णमयीं चैव कण्ठमालामदाद् विभुः».

advaita.text: A fourth boon given from pleasure; Śaṅkara’s second sense of the chain — the way of action with its many fruits — keeps the verse within the realm of ritual: «अन्यदपि कर्मविज्ञानमनेकफलहेतुत्वात्स्वीकुर्वित्यर्थः».

visistadvaita.text: The plain sense: the fire will be known as the Nāciketa, «नाचिकेतः इति प्रसिद्धो भविता», and the chain is a gift.

dvaita.text: The same plain sense; the chain is a golden necklace, «शृङ्कां स्वर्णमयीं चैव कण्ठमालामदाद् विभुः».

schools.disagreement: No doctrinal disagreement; only Śaṅkara offers the second, figurative sense of the chain.

contemporary.text: Death gives more than was asked, because the student learned well. Generous teachers and leaders still do this: they name the work after the one who made it possible. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: Has anyone ever given you more than you asked for, because of how you worked?
reflect.deeper: What is the difference between a reward and a recognition?
reflect.practice: Today, credit someone by name for something they made possible.

flags.note: dadāmi (base) against dadāni (Madhva’s text, Raṅgarāmānuja); Madhva’s text spells the chain śṛṅkā (spelling only).
